newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Hui Shung to tender 54,500T U.S. soy/corn.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Hui Shung to tender 54,500T U.S. soy/corn.

text.p: Taiwan's Hui Shung Group will tender on Friday for a combined shipment comprising 38,500 tonnes of U.S. soybeans and 16,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 corn, local traders said on Thursday.
Taiwan traders expected to see a strong U.S. soybean price in the near term, saying it could test US$8.00 per bushel.
"The soybean is very strong now and I would not be surprised to see U.S. soybeans top US$8.00 per bushel," a trader said.
The March CBOT soybean contract closed at $7.45-1/2 on Wednesday, the highest since October 10.
"We can only hope that Brazilian soybean production will not be hindered by weather," he added.
Forecasts have called for temperatures of 5-10 degrees F above normal in Brazil's key soybean growing areas, which could stunt the crop and push prices even higher.

The Taichung and Kaoshung divisions of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association are likely to take Hui Shung Group's cue and place their own tenders next week for up to 216,000 tonnes of soybeans in total, traders said.
The Hui Shung Group includes Hui Shung Agriculture and Food Corp, Eagle Food Industry and Charoen Pokphand.
Taiwan's food processing industry has a huge appetite for soybeans, importing an estimated 2.4 million tonnes in 1996.
Details for the Hui Shung Grop tender are as follows: Corn 16,000 U.S. Gulf Pacific N.W.
